title: CRLR/143/2017 of Manoj Kumar Vs Smt. Mani mani Marwah AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 143 of 2017
Manoj Kumar ÖÖ.Revisionist
Vs.
Smt. Mani and another ÖÖ.Respondents
Mr. Vikas Kumar Guglani, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. Siddhartha Srivastava, Brief Holder for the State.
Mr. Gopal K. Verma, Advocate for respondent no. 1.

Honíble Lok Pal Singh, J.
The matter was listed today and parties were
present. They were sent for mediation. As per the report
of the Mediator, there is no chances of amicable
settlement between the parties and mediation proceeding
is closed as unsuccessful.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties on merits.

3. Present criminal revision has been preferred against
the order dated 03.03.2017 passed by the Principal
Judge, Family Court Dehradun in criminal case no. 52 of
2015 Mani and another vs. Manoj Kumar whereby the
learned Judge has awarded an amount of ` 5,000/- as
interim maintenance in the favour of wife and ` 2,000/-
per month interim maintenance in the favour of minor
son.
4. Brief facts of the case are that respondent Smt.
Mani got married to revisionist Manoj Kumar on
12.10.2011 as per the Hindu Rites. One son was born
out of the wed-lock. It appears that the relations between
the husband and wife got soured whereafter an
application under section 125 Cr.P.C., was moved by the
wife before the Principal Judge, Family Court, Dehradun,
in which the present revisionist (husband) was directed

2
to pay interim maintenance @ ` 5000/- per month to the
wife and ` 2000/- per month to minor son. Said
application was contested by the revisionists stating that
the income of the revisionist is only ` 5,000/- to `
6,000/- per month. However, the Magistrate after hearing
the parties directed the present revisionist to pay interim
maintenance @ ` 7000/- per month to the respondent
(with whom a minor son was also living).
5. Learned counsel for the revisionists argued that
without assessing the income of the revisionists the
learned court below has arbitrarily directed the present
revisionists to pay interim maintenance @ `7,000/- per
month to the respondents.
6. On the query of the Court, the revisionist has fairly
admitted that he is earning ` 10,000/- per month.
7. Having considered submission of the learned
counsel for the parties, and after perusal of the paper on
record, the order dated 03.03.2017 passed by Principal
Judge, Family Court, Dehradun is modified to the extent
that revisionist shall pay ` 4,000/- per month to
respondent no. 1 and ` 2000/- per month to respondent
no. 2 as interim maintenance (in toto ` 6,000/-).
8. With this modification in the impugned order this
revision stands disposed of with the observation that this
order shall not prejudice the rights of the parties which
are yet to be finally determined after recording of
evidence by the Magistrate concerned.
 (Lok Pal Singh, J.)
Parul 02.07.2018
